capabilities: Sync vault notes into an entity-and-relationship knowledge graph with vector embeddings
Answer questions in a sidebar chat with citations linking back to source notes
Expose MCP tools so external agents can query, search, and write to the vault
Suggest [[wikilinks]] as ghost text while typing, driven by graph entity matches
Highlight cited entities and dim other nodes in Obsidian's native graph view
extras: Manifest carries an unreviewed-plugin warning. Cloud mode uses HangarX's hosted API (no LLM key needed) while local mode runs Docker containers with your own keys; the plugin also polls a /health endpoint every 30 seconds while the chat or stats panel is open.
motivation: The author argues the bottleneck isn't capturing knowledge but making it usable by the agents used every day, since Claude Desktop and Cursor each forget decisions and repeat context.
problem: Obsidian's search can't answer questions, and AI agents have no persistent memory of vault content, so users re-explain their projects in every new chat.

relations.evidence: One-click connect to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf
One-click connect to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf

requires.name: MCP agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) and Docker Desktop for local mode

summary: Vault-to-AI-memory plugin that syncs notes into a knowledge graph, answers questions with citations, and exposes MCP tools to agents like Claude and Cursor.
